articles.title_orig: Stocks plunge as election outcome and AI worries crush tech shares
articles.title_zh: Stocks plunge as election outcome and AI worries crush tech shares
articles.content_orig:
BREAKING: Trump’s D.C.-area arch approved by federal planning commission as court battle looms
Stocks plummeted Thursday, as a blue wave of victories by anti-AI candidates from Maine to Alaska added to already growing fears about the durability of the artificial intelligence boom.
The tech-focused Nasdaq 100 index dropped 6.3%, erasing $2.3 trillion in market value, as investors stepped back to evaluate new risks to the billions of dollars in investments that have poured into the AI sector.
The S&P 500 plunged 4.4%, erasing $2.8 trillion from the index’s value. Both indexes suffered their worst day since April 2025, when President Donald Trump’s global tariffs rocked markets.
The broader Nasdaq Composite, which tracks more than just tech stocks, fell more than 5.5% and tumbled into “correction” territory, which is when a stock or index declines at least 10%.
Markets had largely expected Democrats to win majorities in Congress. But they did not anticipate the scale of the victories, or the upset wins of candidates like Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa in Texas, the largest data center market in the country.
Democrats still hope to clinch Senate seats in Mississippi and Alaska. But already, hundreds of candidates who pledged to rein in AI data centers have been elected to office, raising the prospect of increased regulation on an industry that is the primary driver of U.S. economic growth.
Trump weighed in Thursday to blame the plummeting of stocks on Democrats.
“The Stock Market suffered one of the Worst Days in History based on the results of the Election. Such a sad thing to watch!” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social . “It took so much work to get us to a level that no one has ever seen before, and then this. Your 401(k)s have, therefore, dropped. Remember, it wasn’t Republicans, it was Dumocrats. Do not fear, however, we will soon, one way or the other, be BIGGER AND STRONGER THAN EVER BEFORE.”
Tech stocks have surged in recent years as excitement about artificial intelligence has fueled billions of dollars in investments in, and by, the companies that make chips and infrastructure necessary for AI’s development and operation.
Since Election Day 2024, the Nasdaq Composite is still up by more than 30%, despite recent fears that have sharply driven down chip, memory, and other AI- and cloud computing-linked stocks.
But questions about whether AI will enable the kind of productivity necessary to generate returns on those investments have grown louder in recent months.
“I don’t think this is an AI bubble bursting,” said Ed Yardeni, longtime market watcher and president of Yardeni Research. “I think it’s an AI bubble losing some air very, very rapidly, and I think that reduces the likelihood that we’ll get a bursting bubble that has adverse consequences for the economy and broader financial system.”
The selling continued as Asian markets opened on Friday morning local time. Korea’s Kospi index plunged 8%, triggering a market-wide trading halt. AI data center suppliers Samsung and SK Hynix fell by at least 9% in early trading.  Japan’s Nikkei 225 index tumbled 3%.
The commanding Democratic victories across the country in Tuesday’s midterm elections hit investors hard Thursday, after stocks initially rallied, on what many said was relief that the results of the midterms were projected quickly and clearly.
Numerous Democrats who won races for governor, attorney general and Senate and House seats have pledged to slow or halt the construction of AI data centers.
Texas, Ohio, Michigan and Georgia were of particular concern, because they are all large data center markets.
Democrats who won other state and federal offices have also voiced concerns about the industry and its companies.
“Today is the cold shower that I anticipated might occur after a blue-wave situation,” Yardeni said.
Elon Musk’s companies SpaceX and Tesla each slid nearly 10%, largely in response to the midterm results. But the two companies are also engaged in developing AI, and SpaceX has recently emerged as a data center developer.
On paper, both of Musk’s companies have shed more than $400 billion in value since Tuesday’s election results.
Musk, the world’s first trillionaire, spent hundreds of millions to help elect Republican midterm candidates. Until Tuesday’s rout, he was seen as one of the largest potential beneficiaries of Republican victories.
Now that voters have so resoundingly rejected the GOP, Musk and his companies face the prospect of tighter regulation and even potential investigations at both the state and federal levels.
The sell-off was triggered by two lackluster earnings reports from major chipmakers, Qualcomm and Arm Holdings, which were released on Wednesday night. Both companies posted results that investors generally viewed as mixed.
Arm Holdings slid 13%, while Qualcomm tumbled 9.5%.
The Philadelphia semiconductor index sold off by 12.3%, its worst day since March 2020, when the coronavirus pandemic began to shutter the economy. The “DRAM” ETF, which tracks firms that manufacture computer memory, sank almost 18%.
Earnings reports like these have rattled investors in recent months because of the hundreds of billions of dollars that are being poured into the AI sector.
SanDisk shares plummeted 22%, Micron, Western Digital and AMD fell 17%, while Seagate fell 16%. All of those firms were among the worst performing S&P 500 stocks.
Oil prices rebounded from Wednesday’s drop. Brent crude oil ended the day up by 3.8%. U.S. crude oil rose 2.7% on Thursday.
U.S. Treasury yields, which have faced some competition from tech giants tapping the bond markets to raise funds for their AI ambitions, were slightly lower.
In the wake of the market moves, traders dialed back bets that the Federal Reserve would raise rates during its Dec. 8-9 meeting. Odds are currently around 60%.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,833 points or 3.4%. The biggest contributor to the Dow’s drop was Nvidia, which sold off by 9.2%, its largest one-day decline since April 2025.
Nvidia is the most important supplier to any AI firm, but as investors raise questions about returns, the euphoria in the industry is fading. Nvidia’s shares have tanked 15% over the past three months.
Major established cloud computing providers Alphabet, Meta, Amazon and Microsoft also fell, but less than the overall market declines.
Dow components Cisco and Caterpillar, which are both major suppliers to AI data centers, also dropped around 6%.
Steve Kopack is a senior reporter at NBC News covering business and the economy.
Allie Canal is a business reporter for NBC News.

articles.title_orig: Trump Threatens To 'Destroy' Iran, Tehran Sends Nuke Proposal With 7 Terms
articles.title_zh: Trump Threatens To 'Destroy' Iran, Tehran Sends Nuke Proposal With 7 Terms
articles.content_orig:
Iran has called the US response to its seven conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz “unconvincing” as US President Donald Trump confirmed launching strikes on an Iranian island near the strategic waterway.
The developments on Tuesday came as Qatar stepped up diplomatic efforts to avert a renewed war between the US and Iran and as another oil tanker was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz.
The indirect talks centre on an Iranian proposal to reopen the waterway over two days, if the US meets Tehran’s seven demands, including the lifting of sanctions and ending a US naval blockade.
Despite reports of progress in recent days, Mohsen Rezaei , the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said on Tuesday that Washington’s response had fallen short.
“America’s response to Iran’s rights and demands was not convincing, and they must fully and explicitly address Iran’s seven conditions and act upon them,” he wrote on X.
“Only in this case will the Strait of Hormuz be reopened.”
His post came after Majed al-Ansari, a spokesperson for Qatar’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, said that talks were continuing and that both sides “remain committed to the negotiation process “.
He said Qatar was facilitating the “real-time exchange of proposals between” the US and Iran.
In Washington, DC, Trump confirmed the US had struck Iran early on Tuesday, telling Fox News that the strikes had targeted an anti-aircraft facility.
He described the operation as a “minor attack” and said it “wasn’t war”.
“They built an anti-aircraft facility. It took them about two months. We watched it get built. As soon as it was completed, we hit it last night,” he said.
Iranian media said the strikes hit Qeshm Island in the Gulf near the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier in the day, US officials told US media that the strikes had been “defensive” and followed Iranian fire at an American aircraft.
The strikes came as US media, citing US officials, reported that Central Command had prepared plans for strikes that could begin as early as Wednesday, after the midterm elections, when three American aircraft carriers would be in the region.
The crucial elections could cost Trump’s Republicans control of both the House and the Senate, and fears have grown that Trump could carry out a threatened attack on Iran once the vote is over.
US media have previously reported that the planned campaign would be short and intense.
Trump meanwhile repeated warnings of further military action on Tuesday, saying, “I’m not looking to … kill lots of people” and “If we have to, we’ll have to.”
In an earlier interview with the Financial Times, he suggested he was content with the state of the stand-off with Iran. “We seem to be getting everything we want,” the paper quoted him as saying in a six-minute telephone interview.
Iran’s supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, meanwhile ordered the military at the weekend to respond to any threat immediately and without geographical limits, and to update its list of targets.
Iranian officials have suggested that European countries and undersea cables in the Gulf could be targeted.
As officials weighed the possibility of escalation, commercial shipping came under further attack .
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed on Wednesday that four oil tankers were destroyed after striking naval mines while attempting to pass through a prohibited shipping lane south of the Strait of Hormuz.
The tankers remained ablaze following the explosions, the IRGC said in a statement carried by the official IRNA news agency. Two other vessels were detained for violating shipping restrictions, it added.
Earlier, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that two unidentified projectiles struck a tanker’s engine room about 14 nautical miles (26km) northeast of Oman’s coastal village of Limah on Tuesday. No casualties were reported.
It could not be independently verified whether the incidents reported by UKMTO and the IRGC were linked.
The IRGC also claimed its air defence forces shot down a US-made MQ-9 drone over the strait at 4.30am local time (01:00GMT), describing it as the 56th such aircraft it had downed.
The statement said the operations were carried out by the IRGC’s naval and aerospace forces, which had inflicted “heavy blows on the enemy”.
John Mearsheimer, a US political scientist, questioned whether another short bombing campaign could achieve Washington’s objectives, warning that Iranian retaliation could draw the US into a longer confrontation.
“If the 40-day bombing campaign didn’t work, how is the three-day bombing campaign going to work?” he asked in a video commentary, referring to the initial US-Israeli air campaign and proposals for a shorter renewed offensive.
He argued that an Iranian response could prompt further US escalation, increasing the damage to the global economy.

NVDA fell 15% from its October 6 high as 47 AI and chip stocks shed roughly $5 trillion in market value over three weeks.
Hedge funds have cut stock exposure by more than 8% since June, marking their biggest retreat since 2017, and they are now underweight AI for the first time since early 2023.
Goldman Sachs said the sell-off looks closer to its start than its end, with hedge funds' AI holdings still ranking in the top 17% historically.

NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) closed November 2 at $202.06. That was down 1.26% for the day and 15.54% below its October 6 close of $239.24, which was its highest close of the past year. Invesco QQQ Trust ( NASDAQ:QQQ ) fell 1.36% to $681.09, which leaves it 10.34% under its October 6 high of $759.66.
Yahoo Finance counted 47 AI and chip stocks that have lost about $5 trillion in market value since October 6. The biggest losers in Yahoo Finance's count were NVIDIA ($835 billion), Alphabet ( NASDAQ:GOOGL ) ($835 billion), SpaceX ( NASDAQ:SPCX ) ($505 billion) and TSMC ( NYSE:TSM ) ($395 billion), while the 625 other large U.S. stocks in the same count added about $1.3 trillion.
Morgan Stanley runs a prime brokerage desk, which finances and clears trades for hedge funds. Morgan Stanley's data reportedly show funds underweight the broader AI trade for the first time since early 2023, after they cut total stock exposure by more than 8% since June, the biggest retreat since at least 2017, and much of that positioning shift is likely still ahead.

Goldman Sachs data show hedge funds sold AI stocks for five straight days in October, reversing every AI purchase made since the start of 2025. On the biggest day, per Goldman Sachs, they sold shares they owned about 3.5 times faster than they opened new short positions.
A short position profits when a stock falls. Selling existing holdings at that pace looks like de-risking to protect gains more than a bearish call on AI demand.
Underweight means funds hold less of the broad AI trade than their benchmarks do. That usually helps a sell-off end, because fewer holders are left to sell.
Goldman Sachs also said the unwind looks closer to its start than its end. Goldman Sachs data show funds' AI holdings still rank in the top 17% of the past three years, and the Magnificent Seven were net sold in four of the last five trading sessions. A Nomura note put hedge funds' sensitivity to those seven stocks at the 97th percentile as of October 26.
NVIDIA was QQQ's largest holding in the fund's June 30 portfolio filing. That is why the fund fell less than NVIDIA but still fell sharply.
Because the rest of the market rose, money moved around within stocks. After hours on November 2, NVIDIA traded at $203.80 and QQQ at $682.58, slightly above their closes.
Federal Reserve data going back to 1945 show stocks made up a record 48% of household and nonprofit financial assets in the second quarter, up from 39% at the dot-com peak. The richest 10% of households own 88% of stocks.
Those households do much of the country's spending. That is why Bank of America economists called a sustained correction in the AI trade "one of the larger risks to the US and global economy."
NVIDIA's fundamentals look stronger than its recent price action. Second-quarter revenue of $96.22 billion beat the $92.07 billion consensus, and the company guided third-quarter revenue to $108 billion, plus or minus 2%.
NVIDIA is still worth $4.88 trillion, but at roughly 13 times forward earnings, the stock already prices in much of the positioning risk. Crowding in the mega caps is still high, so a weak report on November 17, a date NVIDIA has not yet confirmed, could set off another round of selling.
Even a beat may not end the selling, because if NVIDIA beats estimates and still trades below its November 2 close of $202.06, bearish sentiment and broader market forces can drive the stock lower before a recovery.

articles.title_orig: China, DPRK reaffirm commitment to closer ties
articles.title_zh: China, DPRK reaffirm commitment to closer ties
articles.content_orig:
By ZHAO JIA | 
          China Daily |
          Updated: 2026-11-06 10:09
China and the Democratic People's Republic of Korea have reaffirmed their commitment to deepening friendly ties and sharing experience in party governance, marking the latest in a series of high-level exchanges between the two neighbors.
The commitments were made on Thursday when Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met in Beijing with a Workers' Party of Korea delegation led by Kim Song-nam, a member of the Political Bureau, secretary and international department director of the Central Committee of the WPK.
Wang, a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs, said China stands ready to work with the DPRK to implement the important consensus reached by the top leaders of the two parties and countries, deepen bilateral relations and deliver greater benefits to both peoples.
Close exchanges between President Xi Jinping, who is also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee, and Kim Jong-un, general secretary of the WPK and president of the State Affairs of the DPRK, have guided the continued improvement of bilateral ties, Wang said.
In particular, he said Xi's state visit to the DPRK in June saw the two leaders reach a series of important common understandings, charting the course for bilateral relations in the new era.
Briefing the delegation on the fifth plenary session of the 20th CPC Central Committee, Wang said the most important outcome was the adoption of the resolution on certain major issues concerning persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance.
The resolution carries major immediate significance and provides long-term guidance for strengthening the Party and advancing the building of a strong country and national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, he said.
China stands ready to strengthen exchanges of experience and mutual learning with the DPRK on party and state governance to support the development of both parties and advance the socialist cause in both countries, he added.
Kim Song-nam said the deep friendship and strategic guidance of the two leaders form the fundamental cornerstone of China-DPRK friendship, while socialism is their shared ideal, banner and cause.
Pyongyang is willing to work with Beijing to make tireless efforts to advance China-DPRK friendly relations, he added.
Thursday's meeting came within two weeks after Kim Jong-un paid a visit to Dandong, Liaoning province.
Exchanges and cooperation between the two countries have deepened across various fields over the past two years. Bilateral trade in the first half of this year reached its highest level for the period since 2018.
International passenger train services, Air China flights and operations at land border crossings have all fully resumed this year. The New Yalu River Bridge, opened on Oct 15, is expected to further facilitate trade and people-to-people exchanges.
Yang Danzhi, a research fellow at the National Institute of International Strategy at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, said deepening practical cooperation and exchanges on state governance and party building helps carry forward the revolutionary legacy and traditional friendship between the two parties and countries and opens a new chapter in China-DPRK relations.

articles.title_orig: Wall Street Traders Wrong-Footed After Bullish Equity Calls
articles.title_zh: Wall Street Traders Wrong-Footed After Bullish Equity Calls
articles.content_orig:
A sudden wave of selling swept through U.S. equities on Thursday as hedge funds kept dumping tech XLK positions and anxiety over physical infrastructure constraints sparked a broad retreat across the semiconductors SMH .
The meltdown was broad across the major indexes, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite COMP bearing the brunt of the retreat, plunging 5.4%. The S&P 500 ( SP500 ) dropped 4.1%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJI declined 3.2%.
Just a day after logging one of its busiest trading days of the year—when markets rallied on the outcome of the midterm elections, which delivered a major victory for Democrats in both the Senate and the House of Representatives—Goldman Sachs’ equities desk observed a market suddenly devoid of buyers and dominated by top-down macro selling.
Long-only institutional investors remained frozen on the sidelines following heavy de-risking into midterms, while hedge funds actively offloaded hyperscaler MSFT AMZN GOOG GOOGL META holdings purchased just a day prior, Goldman partner John Flood wrote in an intraday note.
The wide selloff drove heavy volume spikes relative to 20-day averages—up 160% in the State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF SPY , 150% in the VanEck Semiconductor ETF SMH , 100% in the Invesco QQQ Trust QQQ , and 75% in DRAM DRAM -related products—compounded by a second straight day of heavy retail selling skews, the note said.
